title: My food diary
writingModel: Today is Monday and I want to write about my food diary for the whole day. I think it is very important to eat well as a university student. When I eat some nutritious food, I can concentrate better in my Biology lectures. When I don't eat any breakfast, I feel tired and I can't focus. So I always try to eat three meals a day at the WKU cafeteria.

For breakfast this morning, I had some oat porridge with a little honey, some fresh bread with butter, and some black Kazakh tea with milk. I also drank some orange juice. I don't eat any fried food in the morning — I prefer something light and warm. I had breakfast at 7:15 with Ruslan. He had some scrambled eggs and some green tea. Neither of us ate any sweets or any biscuits — we save those for the weekend!

For lunch, there was some delicious shurpa in the cafeteria today — a rich lamb soup with vegetables. I had a bowl of that, some mashed potatoes with chicken, and some fresh cucumber salad. There wasn't any beshbarmak today — that is only on Fridays! I drank some compote with my lunch. How much did the meal cost? Only 600 tenge — very affordable! I don't eat any fast food for lunch because there isn't any on the campus menu.

In the afternoon, I had a small snack between my lectures. I ate some apple slices and drank some mineral water. I didn't eat any chips or any chocolate — I try to avoid any sugary snacks during the week. Ruslan had some grapes from the market — he always brings some fruit to share. How many grapes did he bring? About thirty! We shared them between lectures and felt much more energetic.

For dinner this evening, I had some pasta with tomato sauce and some mixed vegetable salad. I didn't eat any meat for dinner — I prefer lighter food in the evenings. I drank two glasses of water and some herbal tea before bed. How much water do I drink in total every day? About six glasses — my Biology teacher says that is the minimum for good health. My favourite dish of the whole day was the shurpa at lunch — there is some warmth in a good bowl of soup that makes university life feel a little more like home!
